messages.text: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at Cheltenham

metadata.summary: Pioneer Pete could have the County Hurdle back at Cheltenham in March as a target after continuing his charge up the two-mile hurdling rankings in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle.
metadata.content: Cheltenham: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at November meeting | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Cheltenham: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at November meeting Pioneer Pete continued his ascent up the two-mile hurdling rankings when taking top honours in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle under Jonjo O'Neill Jr; Tennessee Tango was second, with Morning Mayhem third. Sunday 15 November 2026 16:52, UK Image: Jonjo O'Neill Jr celebrates aboard Pioneer Pete Pioneer Pete could have the County Hurdle back at Cheltenham in March as a target after continuing his charge up the two-mile hurdling rankings in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle. Posting a fourth win on the spin and backing up his impressive Welsh Champion Hurdle win at Chepstow, the likeable five-year-old was always in the front rank under Jonjo O'Neill Jnr and came clear to win by six and a half lengths at 7-2 from Tennessee Tango. Victory for O'Neill, winning on the horse for the fifth time and riding for his father-brother training combination of Jonjo and AJ O'Neill, put welcome gloss on a day in which he had fallen twice from three previous rides. "I thought Chepstow was his limit, but he is an amazing little horse," said O'Neill senior. "I have no idea how much more is left in the locker, but he is a horse in form and you would have to look at all those options like the County Hurdle now." metadata.summary: Johnny Fisher is looking to return to action early in 2027 and wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua mega-fight.
metadata.content: Johnny Fisher wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua, early next year | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Johnny Fisher wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua, early next year Kristian Prenga almost knocked out Anthony Joshua in his tune up fight before Tyson Fury; Johnny Fisher now wants to test himself against Prenga early in 2027; Watch Aaron McKenna vs Jevgenijs Aleksejevs on Friday December 4 live on Sky Sports John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Sunday 15 November 2026 17:41, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment Anthony Joshua sealed victory over Kristian Prenga with a huge second-round knockout. Courtesy of DAZN Johnny Fisher is looking to return to action early in 2027 and wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua mega-fight. In July, Prenga boxed Joshua in what was meant to be a tune-up fight for the former world champion. Instead Prenga put him down heavily twice in their first round. He was on the edge of victory only for Joshua to storm back and knock him out in the second round. Prenga caught the eye of the boxing world in that fight and Fisher would like the man who almost beat Joshua to be his next opponent. messages.text: Andreeva storms to WTA Finals title without dropping a set

metadata.summary: Mirra Andreeva concluded a stunning week with a second victory over Elina Svitolina to claim the WTA Finals title.
metadata.content: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina as she storms to WTA Finals title without dropping a set: 'It's something unbelievable' | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina as she storms to WTA Finals title without dropping a set: 'It's something unbelievable' Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 to win the WTA Finals; They were playing each other for the second time in the tournament after Andreeva's dominant win over Svitolina in the group stage; Svitolina was far more competitive in the final but could not derail the teenager Monday 16 November 2026 00:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WTA Finals match between Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina Mirra Andreeva concluded a stunning week with a second victory over Elina Svitolina to claim the WTA Finals title. The Russian teenager, who laughed off being called a diva by rival Jessica Pegula in a 'hot mic' moment ahead of the tournament, did not drop a set on her singles debut at the season-ending showpiece, finishing with a 7-5 6-3 success. At 19, the French Open champion is the first woman to claim the title before her 20th birthday since compatriot Maria Sharapova 22 years ago.
